overview: DuPont is a Delaware-incorporated advanced-materials and solutions company, headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, that now operates two reportable segments -- Healthcare & Water Technologies and Diversified Industrials -- serving healthcare/medical device, water filtration, construction, aerospace, automotive and industrial end markets. The company is the legacy remainder of the 2017 Dow/DuPont merger after a long series of separations (Dow 2019, Corteva 2019, Nutrition & Biosciences to IFF 2021, Mobility & Materials to Celanese 2022, Delrin to TJC 2023) that culminated most recently in the November 2025 spin-off of its Electronics business as Qnity Electronics, Inc. and the April 2026 sale of its Aramids business to Arclin. DuPont generated continuing-operations net sales of $6.8 billion in FY2025 and operates manufacturing sites in about 20 countries, with roughly 53% of net sales generated outside the U.S. (about 10% from China/Hong Kong).

business_model.summary: DuPont sells engineered materials, components and filtration systems largely on a B2B basis to OEMs, medical device/biopharma companies, water utilities and industrial end-users, construction products distributors, and aerospace/automotive manufacturers. Revenue is predominantly transactional/project-based product sales (not subscription), though certain product lines (reverse-osmosis/ion-exchange filtration elements, medical packaging materials, specialty adhesives) carry recurring, replacement-driven demand tied to installed base and regulatory renewal cycles.

revenue_streams.name: Healthcare & Water Technologies (medical packaging/devices, water filtration & purification)

business_model.customer_type: B2B -- OEMs, medical device and biopharma manufacturers, municipal and industrial water customers, construction/building-products distributors, aerospace and automotive manufacturers
business_model.geographic_mix: International operations approximately 53% of FY2025 continuing-operations net sales (incl. U.S. exports), U.S. & Canada approximately 47%; China/Hong Kong approximately 10% of consolidated net sales; manufacturing sites: U.S. & Canada 48, EMEA 15, Asia Pacific 15, Latin America 4 (82 total)

competitive_position.market_position: Leading/well-established positions in several niche, technically differentiated categories -- e.g., TYVEK medical packaging and protective garments, FILMTEC/AMBERLITE water filtration and ion-exchange resins, and specialty adhesives/lubricants (MOLYKOTE, BETAFORCE) -- rather than a single dominant market share figure across a diversified portfolio

moat_factors.description: ~6,100 patents and patent applications globally (~4,700 tied to continuing operations); technology embedded in regulated, mission-critical applications (medical packaging sterility, water purity) raises switching costs
Long-established brands (TYVEK, CORIAN, FILMTEC, MOLYKOTE) with customer intimacy built over decades
Medical device and biopharma packaging customers must requalify suppliers through lengthy regulatory approval processes, creating stickiness once designed in

moat_factors.factor: Global manufacturing and local service footprint
moat_factors.description: 82 manufacturing sites across ~20 countries support just-in-time, regionally diversified supply to multinational customers
Scale has shrunk materially after four divestitures since 2021; diversified portfolio no longer anchored by a dominant single business

weaknesses: Much smaller, less diversified company post-Qnity and post-Aramids (~$7B revenue run-rate) than the pre-split entity, reducing scale advantages
Diversified Industrials (building/construction and industrial OEM) is cyclical and exposed to residential/non-residential construction and auto/aerospace production cycles
Legacy PFAS/Chemours liability overhang constrains capital allocation and creates episodic charges unrelated to current operating performance
Relies on continued successful execution of serial portfolio reshuffling (four plus separations/divestitures since 2021) with attendant stranded-cost and TSA complexity

growth_drivers: Secular water-scarcity and water-quality tailwinds driving demand for FILMTEC reverse osmosis/nanofiltration and AMBERLITE ion-exchange resins in municipal, industrial wastewater, desalination, and semiconductor ultrapure-water markets
Aging population and growing complexity of medical devices/biopharma supporting TYVEK medical packaging and Healthcare Technologies (Spectrum, Donatelle) growth
Aerospace build-rate recovery and EV/battery adhesive and structural-bonding content growth within Industrial Technologies

Operating EBITDA margin expansion from a leaner post-separation cost base, the 2026 DuPont Restructuring Program ($100-150 million of expected charges/savings through 2028), and manufacturing productivity -- margin already up from ~22.3% (Q1 2025) to ~25.1% (Q3 2026)
Capital return acceleration: $2 billion share buyback authorization (announced Nov 2025) being executed via successive ASRs/open-market repurchases, supporting EPS growth independent of top-line
Bolt-on M&A in Healthcare Technologies and Water Technologies (Spectrum 2023, Donatelle 2024, Sinochem RO Memtech 2025) to add capacity and capability in core growth niches

business.description: ~11,000+ personal-injury cases pending in the AFFF MDL at year-end 2025 (growing via a 2025 'channeling order'), plus state AG suits (fraudulent-transfer claims tied to the 2015 Chemours separation), Dutch Dordrecht municipal claims and Canadian PFAS cases; DuPont says it never made/sold AFFF but remains a named defendant

An emerging, growing docket of personal-injury (silicosis-type) claims tied to a quartz surfacing product within Diversified Industrials; defense costs already running several million dollars per quarter
Building Technologies exposed to non-residential/residential construction cycles; Industrial Technologies exposed to automotive, aerospace and printing/packaging capex cycles
Company has flagged future impairment risk in the Protection reporting unit given EIDP purchase-accounting carrying values
Fifth major separation/divestiture since 2021 (Qnity spin, Aramids sale) brings stranded costs, TSA dependency and integration/separation risk

financial.description: DuPont remains liable for 56% of MOU-related PFAS costs (Qnity indemnifies the other 44%) and retains contingent tax and 'Stray Liability' exposure from the 2019 Dow/Corteva separations, with no cap on some categories
Largest exposures are EUR, CNY, JPY, CAD and INR; ~53% of sales generated internationally
Investment-grade but mid-BBB/Baa1 ratings (S&P BBB+, Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+, all stable); covenant caps Total Indebtedness/Total Capitalization at 0.60

regulatory.description: Evolving EPA/state health-advisory levels and reference doses for PFAS in drinking water could increase remediation and compliance costs beyond current MOU-shared estimates

China SAMR opened (since suspended) an antitrust probe into the Tyvek business in April 2025; broader U.S.-China tariff/export-control actions and the ongoing IEEPA tariff litigation create uncertainty
If the Qnity Distribution or related internal transactions fail to qualify for tax-free treatment, DuPont could face a significant, largely uncapped tax liability

Ongoing remediation at legacy EIDP sites (Chambers Works, Parlin, Pompton Lakes, Repauno) under the NJ Settlement's remedial-funding-source review process, which could increase required financial assurance

macro.description: Management flagged that military conflict in the Middle East has delayed some water-infrastructure project timing into 2027, though no material financial impact to date
Company relies on third-party suppliers for raw materials/energy; cost pass-through ability varies by end market
Tariff and export-control actions (particularly U.S.-China) could reduce competitiveness or raise costs despite the recent partial IEEPA tariff invalidation

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Water filtration/purification and medical packaging end markets carry secular growth support (water scarcity, aging population, biopharma complexity); industrial/construction end markets are more cyclical and tied to global capex and residential/non-residential construction activity, aerospace build rates and auto production
macro_factors.cyclicality: Mixed -- Healthcare & Water Technologies is relatively defensive/secularly growing, while Diversified Industrials (building products, industrial OEM) is more economically cyclical
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate -- investment-grade issuer with ~$3.1 billion total debt and active interest-rate swap hedging program; capital return program (buybacks) could be curtailed if liquidity access tightens

recent_developments.event: Completed the Electronics Separation via spin-off of Qnity Electronics, Inc. (Nov 1, 2025); received ~$4.1 billion cash distribution from Qnity and repaid ~$4.0 billion of senior notes; Board approved new $2 billion share repurchase authorization (Nov 6, 2025)
Committed to the 2026 DuPont Restructuring Program, expecting $100-150 million of pre-tax restructuring/cost-savings charges through 2028
Completed the Aramids Divestiture to Arclin (TJC LP affiliate) for ~$1.2 billion cash, a $300 million note receivable, and a $325 million non-controlling equity stake
Effected a 1-for-3 reverse stock split (effective June 24, 2026), stated to align per-share metrics with U.S. industrial peers following the shrinkage of the share base from recent divestitures
Final Judicial Consent Order entered for the ~$875 million (DuPont NPV share ~$311 million) New Jersey PFAS settlement; first annual payment of $71 million made in September 2026
Reached a $455 million (DuPont NPV share ~$127 million), 15-year settlement with the State of North Carolina and local municipalities over PFAS claims tied to the Fayetteville Works site

Reported Q3 2026 results: net sales of $1.9 billion (+4% YoY, +5% organic), adjusted EPS of $2.09 vs. ~$1.87 consensus; raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $7.47-$7.52 (from $7.17-$7.32) and announced a planned $250 million Q4 2026 share buyback

items.notes: Raised during 2026 as organic growth (volume + price) outperformed in both segments; FY2025 continuing-operations base was $6,849 million
Raised from $7.17-$7.32 following the Q3 2026 beat; figures are post 1-for-3 reverse stock split
Above the ~$1.87 consensus estimate at the time of guidance
Represents 150-200 bps of expansion vs. baseline; actual margin reached 24.6% in Q1 2026 (from 22.3% in Q1 2025) and 25.1% in Q3 2026 (+80 bps YoY)
Q3 2026 organic sales growth of 5% (Healthcare & Water +4%, Diversified Industrials +5%) ran ahead of this medium-term framework
Supported by margin expansion plus share buybacks

items.target: >90% (medium-term); cumulative $2.7-2.8 billion FCF over three years
items.notes: Q3 2026 free cash flow conversion reported at 121%
Per FY2025 10-K guidance; actual capex for the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026 was $249 million (cash basis)
Under the $2 billion Authorization approved Nov 2025; ~$889 million remained available as of Sept 30, 2026 after ASR/OMR activity in Q2-Q3 2026
On top of regular funding; to be paid from existing cash or other liquidity sources

guidance.management_commentary: Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for a third consecutive quarter following the Q3 beat, citing organic growth strength in both segments and continued manufacturing productivity/margin expansion. Management noted some Middle East water-infrastructure project timing may slip into 2027 but characterized overall demand as broadly similar heading into early 2027, with continued margin expansion and productivity gains; formal 2027 guidance is expected on the Q4 2026 earnings call.

bull_case: Simplified, more focused portfolio post-Qnity spin-off and Aramids sale concentrated in secularly supported Healthcare & Water Technologies and higher-value Diversified Industrials niches
Clear, executing margin-expansion story -- Operating EBITDA margin up from ~22% to ~25%+ within about a year, with further 150-200bps of medium-term expansion targeted

Aggressive, well-funded capital return program ($2 billion buyback authorization being executed via successive ASRs, consistent $0.60/share quarterly dividend) supported by >90% free cash flow conversion targets

Several of the largest legacy PFAS liabilities (Water District, Ohio, Delaware, New Jersey, North Carolina) have now been converted from open-ended litigation risk into fixed, multi-year payment schedules shared under the MOU, reducing (though not eliminating) tail-risk uncertainty
Track record of beating and raising guidance through 2026, with Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.09 well ahead of the ~$1.87 consensus
bear_case: Material unresolved PFAS/AFFF litigation overhang remains -- more than 11,000 personal-injury cases pending and growing, plus fraudulent-transfer claims, Dutch and Canadian matters not covered by the NJ/NC settlements, with liabilities DuPont says it 'is unable to estimate' above current accruals

Company is now substantially smaller (~$7.2 billion revenue run-rate) and less diversified after shedding the higher-growth Electronics business and Aramids, concentrating results in more cyclical construction/industrial end markets

China/trade exposure (SAMR Tyvek antitrust probe, ~10% of sales from China/Hong Kong, ongoing U.S. tariff and export-control uncertainty including unresolved IEEPA tariff litigation) creates episodic headline and margin risk

Stock has rallied sharply in 2026 (helped by a 1-for-3 reverse split and repeated guidance raises); analyst price targets show wide dispersion, suggesting the self-help/margin story may already be substantially priced in

Continued complexity and cost from serial portfolio restructuring (five separations/divestitures since 2021, TSA dependencies with Qnity, stranded corporate costs, an active multi-year restructuring program) create ongoing execution risk
